newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel sees deal on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel sees deal on stability pact.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told German television on Monday he thought European leaders meeting in Amsterdam would reach agreement on a fiscal stability pact to ensure discipline after the euro launch.
"We will agree, you will see," Kinkel told German ZDF television in a live link from Amsterdam, where the pact will be a top issue at the two-day EU summit. "If not today, then tomorrow," he said.
But Kinkel reiterated Germany's opposition to a Europe-wide job creation scheme, a sticking point in talks with France.
"We are against a job creation programme on the European level that will cost a lot of money," Kinkel said, adding that such programmes should be undertaken at the national level.

But Kinkel said he understood the new Socialist-led government in France needed to stick to their election promises, that growth and jobs must be given the same importance as the stability pact limiting budget deficits.
Kinkel also said he was sure the planned European economic and monetary union (EMU) would start on time in 1999 and that the entry criteria would be strictly adhered to.
